source.title: Layer-Targeted Multilingual Knowledge Erasure in Large Language Models
source.authors: Taoran Li; Varun Chandrasekaran; Zhiyuan Yu

record.file_problem: none; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures cross-language representational alignment and argues that it is localized by model depth and architecture, refining a broad convergence claim. It does not test convergence between independently trained models as they scale.
record.gate_note: The paper reports layerwise CKA and LRDS analyses of multilingual representations. The layer-wise CKA curves are shown as figures without per-layer numeric values; the identified regions and threshold values are also summarized in Table 5. Unlearning accuracy and Logit Lens results are not included as rows because they measure unlearning outcomes, not representational convergence itself.
record.test_reason: The study uses within-model cross-language CKA and LRDS as a tool to pick layers for unlearning, then reports its own method's erasure and retention. It never compares representations across independently trained models, seeds, modalities or scales, so its results do not bear on any version. Cross-lingual alignment of one model's own representations is a related but different construct, recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors' central conclusion is that intervention depth determines whether multilingual unlearning generalizes: shallow layers collapse held-out-language utility, and deep layers fail to erase. Targeting intermediate, CKA-LRDS-identified language-agnostic layers enables erasure across languages while optimizing on only three source languages. Logit Lens results are taken as evidence of genuine removal rather than output suppression.
record.recipe_differences: Uses within-model cross-language CKA and LRDS layer analyses to identify language-agnostic regions. It does not compare independently trained models for convergence as scale or capability increases.
record.method_sensitivity: Layer depth changes the measured alignment and specificity; varying α by ±0.5 changes some region boundaries, although the chosen target layers remain within the regions tested.

fits_no_version.finding: Within single LLMs (Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen-2.5-7B, BLOOM-7b1), linear CKA between the same chemistry questions in different languages peaks in intermediate layers, and LRDS language specificity is lowest there. The location and range are architecture-dependent: mean CKA is 0.647, 0.512 and 0.642 respectively, and the regions sit at layers 8–23, 19–24 and 5–22.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within a multilingual LLM, representations of the same content in different languages converge in intermediate layers and diverge in early and late layers.

record.problems: Only three model architectures are analyzed, and the alignment analysis uses a specified multilingual chemistry dataset. The paper does not report uncertainty for the alignment results or compare a broad set of alternative similarity measures. Per-layer CKA/LRDS curves are figures without per-layer numeric values. The authors also state that the same data are used for fine-tuning, layer identification, and evaluation.
record.rows_left_out: Unlearning accuracy and Logit Lens results across models, languages, layers, and algorithms were omitted because they measure erasure or retention rather than representational convergence (Tables 1–4 and 7–13).

untested.parts: No comparison of independently trained models, and no scale or capability sweep.
No vision-language models or paired image-caption data.
No mapping, stitching or relative-representation test between models.
No cross-model analysis of features or circuits.
There is no cross-model convergence measurement whose dependence on metric, settings or inputs could be assessed. The α variation concerns the method's layer selection.
No cross-model alignment level, plateau, or causal attribution to shared data or objectives.

record.verdict_notes: This is an unlearning-methods paper. CKA and LRDS serve only to select layers. The 'convergence' it discusses is cross-lingual convergence inside one model, not convergence across models. The reader's T5 tests/V6 limits_scope label is removed. The α thresholds were hand-tuned per architecture by inspecting the curves. The same data are used for fine-tuning, layer identification and evaluation.

versions.untested_parts: No scale or capability sweep, or comparison of independently trained models with different architectures, objectives, or data.
No vision-language models or paired images and captions.
No comparison across random initializations or analysis of shared features or subspaces across seeds.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired interchangeability test between models.
No analysis of recurring interpretable features or circuits across models.

The study varies layer and the LRDS threshold factor α, but does not compare a broad range of similarity measures, vary the number of neighbours, or test out-of-distribution inputs. Its representation analysis uses multilingual chemistry data and three model architectures.
No test of whether shared training data or objectives cause cross-model convergence, nor a cross-model convergence plateau analysis.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-8B
rows.operation_detail: Measured layerwise multilingual CKA and LRDS to identify the joint language-agnostic region.

conditions.value: MMLU and MMMLU High School Chemistry
source languages; average pairwise CKA across supported languages

rows.measure: Joint CKA-alignment and LRDS-specificity region across layers
rows.note: The paper reports layerwise curves in Figure 2 and selects an intermediate region using both metrics; it does not provide numeric values for every layer.
rows.check: Within-model cross-language alignment in Llama-3.1, not convergence between models. Λ = Layers 8–23 is a selection output of the MUTE method, chosen with a tuned α, so it is a selection value, not a result on any version.

reader_labels.condition: Layerwise analyses across the three tested architectures and α sensitivity settings
reader_labels.reason: Alignment is localized to model-specific intermediate layer regions, and changing α can alter region boundaries; however, the selected target layers remain in the regions across tested α values. Rows r1–r6.
